newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S. applauds leftist turn in El Salvador.
newsitem.headline: U.S. applauds leftist turn in El Salvador.

text.p: A senior U.S. official called the big gains made by El Salvador's former guerrillas in Sunday's mid-term elections a step forward for democracy.

The Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front (FMLN) won the mayoral race in the capital, San Salvador, and a solid block of seats in Congress in a major setback for the ruling right-wing Republican National Alliance (ARENA) party.

"If the FMLN did well, so be it. It's a democratic process where everybody gets a chance to run and get elected," Assistant Secretary of State for Inter-American Affairs Jeffrey Davidow said late on Monday during a visit to Panama.
Davidow applauded the transition made by the FMLN from guerrilla movement to mainstream political party after signing a peace agreement with ARENA in 1992.

"I'm proud, to whatever degree we can help, to support that system," Davidow told Reuters. "The parties realised they did not have to fight, that there was a democratic process they could take advantage of; that's excellent," he said.

"The big problem the FMLN is going to have with governing San Salvador is the problem every municipal government has. They're not going to be worried about ideology or other grand political issues, they've got to collect the garbage and make sure the city provides services, and that's good."

Results tallied on Monday showed the FMLN had won at the ballot box what it had failed to win at gunpoint, gaining 34.2 percent of the votes, almost defeating President Armando Calderon's ARENA party, which polled 35.4 percent.

The FMLN was widely considered Latin America's most professional guerrilla army in El Salvador's civil war, which was the bloodiest in Central America at the time. But after laying down its arms, the FMLN lost elections in 1994 to Calderon who swept to victory by nearly a two-to-one margin.
